# s222 — Pack current trusted notes for the selected item

Pickup can load a bounded set of current notes from the selected item without changing complete audit reads or deterministic generated documents.

**Findings:** agents feedback 2026-10-05 U12b; docs/feedback/agents-2026-10-05.md · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-06** — Ready for review: added read-only current note packs to show and next --ready, including section/context and batch projections. --min-trust/--notes-budget opt into expiry filtering; ranking uses verification trust, creation time and stored order; whole display notes share per-item Unicode budgets with oversize skipping. note_pack records selected IDs and deterministic omission reasons, survives lean including empty manifests, and covers stable legacy slice IDs. Ordinary/kind-only reads and generated documents remain complete. Added 15 packing tests and command/agent documentation. Full unittest discovery: 1401 tests, OK (1 skipped); tracking check and git diff --check pass.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** dependency-neighborhood retrieval, embeddings or catalogs, writing state during a read, filtering acceptance based on trust, or silently dropping expired notes from ordinary reads.

## Why

The owner selected item-local packs, opt-in expiry filtering, whole-note budgeting, and explicit verification tiers. U3's kind selection remains useful independently and must compose with packing.

## Files

A stdlib pure note-selection helper, CLI show/next-ready including batch output, note-pack tests and command/agent documentation. Rendering of committed files remains clock-independent.

## Failing tests

- Without min-trust or notes-budget, ordinary show/ready reads keep every note, including expired notes; kind-only filtering does not activate expiry filtering.
- Either packing option excludes notes whose stale_after <= the captured read time, combines OR kind selection with minimum trust, and returns manifest reasons.
- Higher trust precedes lower trust, newer known created_at precedes older/unknown dates, and stored order resolves equal ties. Explicit verification tier changes affect selection, not authorship alone.
- Whole display notes plus newline separators fit exactly within the character budget; oversized notes are skipped and later fitting notes remain eligible. Unicode code points, zero budget and empty results behave deterministically.
- Show, next-ready, section projections, lean output and batch-ready apply the same policy; each selected batch item gets its own budget. Unknown trust values/negative budgets fail before --start writes.
- Legacy item and slice notes are untyped/unverified; legacy slice manifest IDs are stable read identifiers. Selection never changes state, render bytes, history or claims on a plain read.

## Implement

Add min-trust with values unverified, machine-confirmed and human-reviewed, and notes-budget as a nonnegative integer. Either option enables packing; omitted trust means unverified and omitted budget means unlimited. On next these options require ready. Existing notes-kind filters combine with them but do not enable packing by themselves.

Capture one UTC read time per invocation. Exclude expired notes at or after stale_after; no expiry is current. Collect selected-item notes only. Rank by descending derived trust, then descending created_at with unknown dates last, then stored order. Use display strings as budgeted texts, counting Python Unicode characters and one newline between selected strings. Keep whole notes; skip an over-budget note and continue. Do not count manifest serialization against the text budget.

Return filtered display-string notes and corresponding item note_records plus note_pack with selected IDs, omitted {id, reason} entries, characters, budget and min_trust. Reasons use deterministic precedence: kind, expired, trust, budget. Always expose a requested pack manifest, including an empty pack under lean. Legacy slice-note IDs use slice-legacy-N in their original order and are read-only; selected legacy text remains in the slice notes projection. Each batch entry has an independent pack sharing the invocation's captured time.

Generated render remains a complete deterministic projection; never evaluate wall-clock expiry there. Document that complete audit reads are the default and no pack operation promotes trust or hides the item/sections.
